newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Sellers look to US for jet sales.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Sellers look to US for jet sales.

text.p: Oil companies and traders in Asia who are holding large jet fuel stocks in storage are seeking possible outlets in the U.S. where small demand might be emerging, traders said on Monday.
""It's possible to move between one and three cargoes there (the U.S. West Coast)," one trader said.
"There has been some interest by a few parties but you (the seller) have to be very sure that you can place the cargoes."
Traders also noted that the demand is not "tremendous" and this did not signal the opening of the floodgates.
"Its possible to move the cargoes if we get the right freight rates," one trader said.

Traders said the situation is exactly the same as that seen a month ago when three gas oil cargoes were moved to South America due to abundant supplies in Asia and the odd requirement that emerged from Argentina and Paraguay.
Traders have said that some two million barrels of jet fuel are in storage in Singapore, and probabaly another 1.5 million barrels in Guam and more in Jebel Ali in the Middle East.

The jet fuel was stored in a contango market as sellers hope for demand to pick up for the winter, but the present low demand is forcing sellers to try to dispose off the stored products to mare way for new production, traders said.

This was reflected in the five offers made on Monday by two US majors, a Swiss trader, a Chinese trader and a European major at between $23.00 and $24.00 per barrel for early September liftings, free-on-board basis.
While the offers were higher than the $22.80 traded on Friday, buyers seemed unimpressed with the higher numbers.
But swaps jet fuel was traded at $24.00

Gas oil also remained under pressure with a 200,000-barrel cargo sold by a Singapore refiner to a Singapore trader at a 40-cent per barrel discount to Singapore spot quotes for September 2-6 lifting, fob basis.

Traders said the loading dates for this cargo was the same as the parcel which the Singapore trader sold to a European major at $22.40 on Friday and might mean that the trader would use the cargo bought on Monday to cover for the earlier sale.
The Singapore trader also made an offer earlier at $22.80 but withdrew it after it bought the 200,000-barrel lot.
Three other offers were made by a US major, a European major and a Mediterranean trader.
Traders said the sentiment in September for gas oil might be as bearish if not worse than in August as China remained absent.
Indonesia would only decide on its September requirements later this week while India's demand would remain soft until after October.
As South Korean refiners return from turnarounds, supplies for September would add on to regional supplies.

They said even if China were to buy more in September with the one-month shutdown of the 160,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) Qilu Petrochemical Co refinery starting August 20, most of the supplies would come from the excess stocks in storage and from South Korea.
Pakistan is expected to issue a tender on Tuesday to buy various oil products for deliveries during the four quarter, a ministry official said.
